proposals.name: Ia-CSM shell interaction
proposals.idea: A thermonuclear explosion began about 24 days ago and rose like a SN Ia, but its ejecta struck a detached hydrogen-rich shell around day -9. The shock adds sustained interaction luminosity, especially H-alpha in r, that arrests the decline and produces the late excess in both bands.

helpers.csm: 0.5 * (1 + tanh((t - t_hit) / t_width)) * (1 - exp(-max(t - t_hit, 0) / t_crise)) * exp(-max(t - t_hit, 0) / t_cdec)

t0.meaning: explosion time in days relative to now

t_peak.meaning: days from explosion to underlying SN peak

t_decl.meaning: underlying SN post-peak decline timescale in days

t_hit.meaning: time ejecta reach the CSM shell

t_width.meaning: width of interaction turn-on in days

t_crise.meaning: interaction luminosity rise timescale in days

t_cdec.meaning: interaction luminosity decay timescale in days

A_sn_b.meaning: peak underlying SN flux per band in microjansky

A_csm_b.meaning: interaction flux scale per band in microjansky, expected larger in r

proposals.predicts: It predicts a weeks-long plateau or slow rebrightening with r persistently above g from shocked H-alpha emission, rather than the smooth post-peak decline expected for a normal Ia, II, or TDE.

proposals.name: Detached CSM shell interaction
proposals.idea: The ejecta from an explosion beginning near t0 have struck a dense, detached circumstellar shell, so shock interaction rather than radioactive decay powers the emission. The growing shocked area produces a slow, red, still-rising light curve until the shock crosses the shell and the interaction luminosity collapses.

amp_b.meaning: peak interaction flux in microjansky for each band

t0.meaning: explosion start time in days relative to now

tau_rise.meaning: shock interaction rise timescale in days

p.meaning: power-law index of the interaction rise

t_shell.meaning: age in days when shock exits the dense CSM shell

w_shell.meaning: width in days of the shell-exit transition

tail_frac.meaning: fraction of peak flux remaining in the post-shell tail

tau_tail.meaning: post-shell exponential decay timescale in days

proposals.predicts: It predicts the flux keeps rising for weeks to a late broad peak near t=+29 d, reddens as it rises, then drops sharply within several days to a faint tail, unlike the smooth decline already predicted by the failed Ia, II and TDE hypotheses.

proposals.name: Delayed Ia-CSM H-alpha interaction
proposals.idea: An initially normal supernova is overtaken after about 17 days by shock interaction with a detached hydrogen-rich circumstellar shell. The interaction adds a slowly rising, long-lived continuum plus strong H-alpha emission that falls in the r band, explaining the late excess and increasing redness missed by single-component Ia, II and TDE models.

helpers.csm_shape: step(t - t_hit) * (1 - exp(-csm_age / tau_csm)) * exp(-csm_age / tau_csm_fall)

sn_b.meaning: peak flux of the underlying supernova in band b

csm_b.meaning: flux scale of CSM interaction in band b, expected much larger in r due to H-alpha

host_b.meaning: constant host galaxy flux in band b

t0.meaning: explosion time in days relative to now

tau_rise.meaning: rise timescale of the underlying supernova in days

age_peak.meaning: age in days at which the underlying supernova peaks

tau_fall.meaning: decline timescale of the underlying supernova in days

t_hit.meaning: time the ejecta reach the detached CSM shell

tau_csm.meaning: turn-on timescale of CSM interaction power in days

tau_csm_fall.meaning: slow decay timescale of CSM interaction in days

proposals.predicts: The r band will remain brighter than g and plateau or rise for weeks before a very slow decline over ~100 days, with g-r continuing to redden, rather than the rapid post-peak fade predicted by the failed single-component hypotheses.
